title: When Microsoft Messaging Looks Secure but Isn’t — Exchange Server, Hybrid and Microsoft 365 Security with Thomas Stensitzki [MVP]
description:
Many Microsoft messaging environments look secure on the surface but still run on defaults, weak identities and misunderstood mail flow. This conversation with Exchange MVP Thomas Stensitzki is for Exchange and Microsoft 365 administrators running on-premises, hybrid or cloud-only email. It covers identity protection, break glass accounts, SPF, DKIM and DMARC, Defender for Office 365 and the operational discipline that keeps messaging secure.
In this episode
00:00 – Introduction to messaging security and the guest04:41 – Exchange Server, Exchange Online and hybrid differences10:11 – Identity, admin roles and break glass accounts15:32 – Legacy authentication and a realistic attack path23:46 – Mail flow, SPF, DKIM and DMARC37:37 – Phishing and Defender for Office 36548:54 – Secure Score, operational discipline and compliance57:48 – AI, Exchange migrations and rapid fire round
Key takeaways
Exchange Online starts with default settings, so mail flow, anti-spam, anti-phishing and anti-malware still need to be configured for the organization's needs.Identity security comes first: protect every user and service account, use PIM for Exchange admins and secure break glass accounts with FIDO keys.Configure SPF, DKIM and DMARC with real policies, use subdomains for third-party senders, and enable Safe Links in Defender for Office 365.
Worth quoting
“Here's a switch on and you can use email but you have to configure it depending on your needs.” – Thomas Stensitzki (07:40)
“So I'd say identity security comes first. So you do have to protect the identity of each user, even though regardless if it's a real person, so a human being or if it's a technical service account” – Thomas Stensitzki (10:18)
